correctness.rationale: Every length-n factor with two or more ones has a unique first adjacent power-gap d. For d>=2 the left-padding count N_d and reversible-pair size S_h yield Q_d, which counts odd integers in (d,2d) bounded by n. Disjoint dyadic intervals enumerate all these classes. The initial gap contributes one class for the canonical word and two after prefixing zero (from n>=4). The same gap counts without reversals give the factor profile. All boundaries n=0,1,2,3 were checked. Standalone independent factor and reversal enumeration: 388 cases; dyadic identity: 65533 lengths. Enumeration corroborates, rather than substitutes for, the all-length counting proof.

value.rationale: Reflection complexity was proposed as a distinct automatic-word invariant and Example 13 in independent research identifies the nonrecurrent powers-of-two indicator as a natural object with known linear-order factor complexity but not an exact reflection count. This theorem gives a complete parity-linear reversal profile and exactly determines the one-sided boundary effect, while the ordinary factor count retains dyadic oscillation and yields sharp ratio limits. It answers a motivated exact-complexity question beyond direct textbook substitutions or a finite census.
